mainTopic: Renting and selling houses and fields to non-Jews in ארץ ישראל, סוריא, and חוץ לארץ, the reasons behind רבי מאיר's and רבי יוסי's rules, and the final הלכה with its שכונה limit.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about renting and selling houses and fields to non-Jews. רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree about what is allowed in ארץ ישראל, in סוריא, and in חוץ לארץ. The משנה adds two limits. A house may not be rented as a home, because עבודה זרה would be brought into it. A bathhouse may not be rented out anywhere, because it is called by the Jewish owner's name. The גמרא explains that fields are treated more strictly than houses because they carry two problems: a foothold in the land and the loss of מעשר. Houses do not lose מזוזה, because מזוזה is the resident's obligation. The גמרא then explains each opinion region by region, using the rule that we do not make a גזירה לגזירה and the dispute over whether כיבוש יחיד counts as a conquest. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, as long as one does not create a non-Jewish שכונה of three people. אביי explains that the first seller is not responsible for what others do later, because the rule covers only direct causing (לפני) and not לפני דלפני. Finally, the גמרא infers from the משנה's wording that there are places where renting is not allowed at all.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's rules for Syria and outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר finishes his view. In סוריא, houses may be rented to non-Jews but fields may not. In חוץ לארץ, houses may be sold and fields may be rented.
steps.simpleTranslation: In Syria, one may rent houses to them but not fields. Outside the Land, one may sell houses to them and rent fields. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing רבי מאיר's list of what a Jew may give non-Jews in each region. The further a place is from ארץ ישראל, the more he allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules become more lenient step by step: strictest in ארץ ישראל, more lenient in סוריא, and most lenient in חוץ לארץ. Fields stay stricter than houses in every region. Selling, which is permanent, is stricter than renting.

phrases.english: one may rent houses to them
phrases.notes: This picks up mid-משנה. רבי מאיר is talking here about סוריא, which was named just before.

phrases.english: but not fields.
And outside the Land,
one may sell houses to them
and rent fields;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר: in סוריא, houses may be rented but fields may not; in חוץ לארץ, houses may be sold and fields may be rented.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's more lenient view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי moves each region one step more lenient. In ארץ ישראל, houses may be rented but fields may not. In סוריא, houses may be sold and fields rented. In חוץ לארץ, both may be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: In the Land of Israel one may rent houses to them but not fields. In Syria one may sell houses and rent fields. Outside the Land one may sell both.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יוסי, who disagrees with רבי מאיר and is more lenient in every region.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allows renting houses even in ארץ ישראל, which רבי מאיר forbade. He gives סוריא the rules that רבי מאיר gave to חוץ לארץ. In חוץ לארץ, he allows full sale of both houses and fields.

keyTerms.meaning: Syria, lands near ארץ ישראל that were conquered by דוד המלך
these and those, meaning both houses and fields

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
In the Land of Israel one may rent houses to them
but not fields.
And in Syria one may sell houses
and rent fields.
And outside the Land one may sell both these and those.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר and is more lenient in each region.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי: in ארץ ישראל, houses may be rented but fields may not; in סוריא, houses may be sold and fields rented; in חוץ לארץ, both may be sold.

steps.title: Renting is never allowed as a residence
steps.stepSummary: Even where renting a house is permitted, it may not be rented as a home, because the non-Jew will bring עבודה זרה into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even where they said one may rent, they did not mean for a living space, because he brings idols into it, as it says: 'Do not bring an abomination into your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to the permission to rent houses: the house may not be rented for someone to live in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The house still counts as the Jew's house. The פסוק forbids bringing something abominable into 'your house.' A non-Jew living there would bring עבודה זרה into the Jew's house.

keyTerms.meaning: a house to live in, a residence
an abomination, here meaning an idol

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the permission to rent houses has been cancelled. The rental is still allowed, but only for uses other than living there, such as storage.

phrases.english: Even in a place where they said one may rent,
they did not say it for a residence,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַכְנִיס לְתוֹכוֹ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: because he brings idol worship into it,
as it says: 'You shall not bring an abomination into your house.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission to rent houses given by both תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house may not be rented to a non-Jew as a residence, because of the rule against bringing a תועבה into one's house.

steps.title: A bathhouse may never be rented out
steps.stepSummary: In every place, a Jew may not rent his bathhouse to a non-Jew, because it is called by the owner's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in any place, one may not rent him the bathhouse, because it is called by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a rule that applies everywhere: a bathhouse may not be rented to a non-Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the concern is what people will think, not עבודה זרה. People know the bathhouse by the Jewish owner's name. When they see it running on שבת, they will think the Jew is running it.

keyTerms.meaning: it is called by his name

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three separate concerns: the region and the type of property (house or field), living in the house (עבודה זרה), and the bathhouse (what people will think).

phrases.english: And in every place,
one may not rent the bathhouse to him,
because it is called by his name.
phrases.notes: People will think the Jewish owner is running it, even on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְכׇל מָקוֹם לֹא יַשְׂכִּיר לוֹ אֶת הַמֶּרְחָץ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bathhouse may not be rented to a non-Jew anywhere, because it is known by the Jewish owner's name.

steps.title: Why are fields 'all the more so' forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means when it says 'needless to say, fields.' Why is the rule for fields more obvious than the rule for houses?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'needless to say, fields'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking about the earlier line of the משנה about ארץ ישראל. It is setting up a search for the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said houses may not be rented in ארץ ישראל, and fields all the more so. The גמרא wants to know what extra problem fields have that houses do not.

keyTerms.meaning: needless to say, all the more so

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is meant by 'needless to say, fields'?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes renting fields more clearly forbidden than renting houses?

steps.title: Suggestion: fields involve two problems
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a field carries two problems. It gives non-Jews a foothold in the land, and it takes the field out of the obligation of מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because a field has two problems: one, giving them a foothold in the land; and one, that it removes the field from tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer, introduced with 'אילימא' (if you say). This word warns us that a challenge is about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Houses have only one problem: a foothold in the land. Fields have a second problem as well. A non-Jew working the field will not separate מעשר, so the land loses that מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (a suggestion that is about to be tested)
giving them a foothold or settlement in the land

phrases.english: If you say it is because it has two problems:
one, giving them a foothold in the land;
and one, that he removes it from the tithe.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fields have two problems, a foothold in the land and the loss of מעשר, while houses have only one.

steps.title: But houses also have two problems
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion. Houses also have two problems: a foothold in the land, and taking the house out of the obligation of מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, houses also have two problems: one, a foothold in the land; and one, that it removes the house from מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested answer. If 'two problems' is the reason, houses should be just as bad as fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house lived in by a non-Jew will not have a מזוזה, just as a field farmed by a non-Jew will not have מעשר taken from it. So the 'two problems' answer does not explain why fields are worse.

keyTerms.meaning: the parchment scroll fixed on a doorpost

phrases.english: If so,
houses also have two problems:
one, a foothold in the land;
and one, that he removes it from mezuzah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי בָּתִּים נָמֵי אִיכָּא תַּרְתֵּי
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that fields are worse because they carry two problems.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Houses carry the same two-part problem, with מזוזה in place of מעשר, so the suggestion does not set fields apart.

steps.title: Mezuzah depends on the resident, not the house
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא answers that מזוזה is an obligation on the person who lives there. Renting a house to a non-Jew takes away nothing that belongs to the house, so houses have only one problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: מזוזה is the obligation of the resident.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא defends the 'two problems' answer by showing that houses really have only one problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר is tied to the produce of the land, so a field farmed by a non-Jew loses that מצוה. מזוזה is an obligation on whoever lives in the house. When no Jew lives there, nobody is obligated, so nothing is lost from the house itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Fields are worse than houses because a field loses מעשר, which is tied to the land. A house does not lose מזוזה, because מזוזה is an obligation on the person living there, not on the house.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic rule about מזוזה: it is an obligation on the resident (חובת הדר), not on the building (חובת הבית).

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
Mezuzah is the obligation of the resident.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא מְזוּזָה חוֹבַת הַדָּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and keeps the 'two problems' explanation in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the nature of the obligation: מזוזה falls on the person, not on the property.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Houses lose מזוזה just as fields lose מעשר, so both carry two problems.
steps.terutzMaskana: מזוזה is the resident's obligation, so a rented house loses nothing. Only fields carry two problems, which is why the משנה says 'needless to say, fields.'

steps.title: Why may houses in Syria be rented but not sold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule for סוריא and asks why selling houses there is forbidden when renting them is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'In סוריא we may rent houses to non-Jews.' What is different about selling houses, that it is not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about סוריא. It asks why selling a house there is forbidden while renting it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting and selling both put a non-Jew in a Jewish house. The גמרא wants to know what makes selling worse, so that the line between them makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Syria, the land north of ארץ ישראל that דוד המלך conquered
what is different? (asks for the reason behind a distinction)

phrases.english: In Syria one may rent houses, etc.
What is different about selling, that it is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of 'needless to say, fields' to the next clause of the משנה, about סוריא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason selling houses in סוריא is forbidden while renting them is allowed.

steps.title: Selling in Syria could lead to selling in Eretz Yisrael
steps.stepSummary: Selling houses in סוריא was forbidden so that people would not come to sell houses in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden because of selling in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ban on selling in סוריא is a protective fence. If people got used to selling there, they might sell in ארץ ישראל too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling a house in ארץ ישראל to a non-Jew is a serious problem, because it gives him a foothold in the land. Because סוריא is so close and so similar, the rabbis made a גזירה against selling there as well.

phrases.english: Because of selling in the Land of Israel.
phrases.notes: He means: the rabbis were worried that selling in סוריא would lead people to sell in ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Selling in סוריא is forbidden as a גזירה, so that people will not come to sell in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Then renting in Syria should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: If we worry that what people do in סוריא will spread to ארץ ישראל, renting houses in סוריא should also be banned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us also make a גזירה against renting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Renting houses is also forbidden in ארץ ישראל, so by the same reasoning it should be forbidden in סוריא as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 10 says the rules of סוריא copy the rules of ארץ ישראל so people don't get confused. But in ארץ ישראל renting houses is also forbidden, so the same reasoning should forbid renting in סוריא. Yet the משנה allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: if so (sets up a challenge from the previous answer)
let us make a גזירה (a rabbinic protective decree)

phrases.english: If so,
let us also issue a decree against renting!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason in step 10: a גזירה in סוריא to protect the rules of ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that reason is valid, it should also forbid renting in סוריא, because renting houses is forbidden in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: We do not make a decree to protect another decree
steps.stepSummary: The ban on renting in ארץ ישראל is itself only a גזירה, and the rabbis do not add a second גזירה just to protect a first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule itself is a גזירה. Should we get up and make a גזירה to protect a גזירה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that renting houses in ארץ ישראל is forbidden only as a fence against selling. Banning renting in סוריא would be a fence around a fence, and the rabbis do not do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling in ארץ ישראל is the real problem, so a fence in סוריא to protect it makes sense. Renting in ארץ ישראל is already just a fence, so a ban on renting in סוריא would be a גזירה לגזירה, which is not done. That is why renting is allowed in סוריא and selling is not.

keyTerms.meaning: a decree made to protect another decree (a fence around a fence)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of not making a גזירה לגזירה comes up all over ש״ס. It explains why the rabbis' fences usually stop after one layer.

phrases.english: It itself is a decree,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ban on renting houses in ארץ ישראל, which only exists so that people won't come to sell.

phrases.english: and shall we arise and decree
a decree for a decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: הִיא גּוּפַהּ גְּזֵרָה, וַאֲנַן נֵיקוּם וְנִיגְזוֹר גְּזֵרָה לִגְזֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference in how many layers of decree are involved
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any rule of ארץ ישראל should be copied in סוריא, renting included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only rules based on a real problem are copied in סוריא. Renting is already a גזירה, and we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: But renting fields in Syria is a decree on a decree
steps.stepSummary: Renting fields in סוריא is forbidden, even though renting fields in ארץ ישראל is itself only a גזירה. That looks like a גזירה לגזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But renting a field in סוריא is a גזירה for a גזירה, and still we forbid it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule it just stated. The משנה forbids renting fields in סוריא, which seems to be exactly the kind of double גזירה the rabbis supposedly avoid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל renting a field to a non-Jew is forbidden only as a fence. So banning it in סוריא too would be a גזירה לגזירה, yet the משנה does ban it. This shows the rule from step 12 cannot be the whole story.

phrases.english: But renting a field in Syria,
which is a decree for a decree,
and yet we do issue the decree!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא שְׂכִירוּת שָׂדֶה דִּבְסוּרְיָא, דִּגְזֵרָה לִגְזֵרָה הִיא, וְקָא גָזְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle used in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids renting fields in סוריא, which looks like a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: Syria counts as conquered land, so this is not a double decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds כיבוש יחיד שמיה כיבוש, so סוריא has the status of conquered land and its rules are not just a fence around a fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is not just a גזירה, because he holds that a conquest by an individual counts as a conquest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in סוריא we are not dealing with a simple double גזירה. רבי מאיר holds that the conquest of סוריא counts, so the land has some of the status of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סוריא really counts as conquered land, then banning things there is not 'a גזירה to protect a גזירה' made from far away. The rules apply to the land of סוריא itself. That removes the challenge of step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: a conquest by an individual (not by the whole nation together)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean סוריא is exactly the same as ארץ ישראל. It means its conquest counts enough that its rules are not just a double גזירה. The next step shows the rabbis still treat fields and houses differently there.

phrases.english: There it is not merely a decree,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the rules for סוריא. They are not just a fence protecting the rules of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he holds: the conquest of an individual is called a conquest.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי מאיר, the author of this משנה. סוריא was conquered by דוד המלך on his own, and he holds that it still counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָאו גְּזֵרָה הוּא, קָסָבַר: כִּיבּוּשׁ יָחִיד שְׁמֵיהּ כִּיבּוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the rule in סוריא is not a double גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidding field rentals in סוריא is a גזירה לגזירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because כיבוש יחיד שמיה כיבוש, סוריא has its own status, so its rules are not a double גזירה.

steps.title: Fields have two problems, so the rabbis were stricter
steps.stepSummary: Fields carry two problems, so the rabbis forbade renting them in סוריא. Houses carry only one problem, so the rabbis did not forbid renting them there.
steps.simpleTranslation: A field, which has two problems, the rabbis made a גזירה about. Houses, which do not have two problems, the rabbis did not make a גזירה about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the rule for סוריא. It uses the 'two problems' idea from earlier to explain why fields and houses are treated differently there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said a field has two problems: a foothold in the land and losing the obligation of מעשר. A house has only the foothold problem, since מזוזה belongs to the person who lives there. So the rabbis forbade renting fields in סוריא but allowed renting houses.
steps.whatToRemember: In סוריא: houses may be rented but not sold, and fields may not be rented. Fields are treated more strictly because they carry two problems, and houses carry only one.

phrases.english: A field, which has two problems —
the Sages issued a decree about it,
houses, which do not have two problems —
the Sages did not issue a decree about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂדֶה דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי — גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 14 by explaining the difference between fields and houses in סוריא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In סוריא the rabbis forbade renting fields, which carry two problems, but did not forbid renting houses, which carry only one.

steps.title: Outside the land, fields may not be sold but houses may
steps.stepSummary: The same 'two problems' reasoning explains the משנה's rule for חוץ לארץ: selling fields is forbidden, while selling houses is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Outside the land, etc.' A field, which has two problems, the rabbis made a גזירה about. Houses, which do not have two problems, the rabbis did not make a גזירה about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last part of the משנה, about חוץ לארץ. It explains that rule with the same reasoning it just used for סוריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, outside the land you may sell houses and rent fields, but you may not sell fields. Fields in ארץ ישראל carry two problems, so the rabbis forbade selling them even in חוץ לארץ. Houses carry only one problem, so the rabbis left their sale allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: etc. (the rest of the quoted line)

steps.whatToRemember: One principle runs through רבי מאיר's whole משנה: fields, with their two problems, get stricter rules than houses, which have only one. This is true in ארץ ישראל, in סוריא, and in חוץ לארץ.

phrases.english: Outside the Land, etc.
A field, which has two problems —
the Sages issued a decree about it,
houses, which do not have two problems —
the Sages did not issue a decree about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 15 to the next clause of the משנה, about חוץ לארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In חוץ לארץ the rabbis forbade selling fields, which carry two problems, but did not forbid selling houses, which carry only one.

steps.title: Why does רבי יוסי allow renting houses in ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's first rule from the משנה and asks for its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: In ארץ ישראל we may rent houses to them, and so on. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי יוסי's opinion in the משנה. It quotes his first rule and asks why it is so, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allows renting houses in ארץ ישראל, but not fields. The גמרא wants to know why houses and fields are treated differently.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַשְׂכִּירִין לָהֶם בָּתִּים וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: In Eretz Yisrael one may rent houses to them, etc.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי מאיר's opinion to רבי יוסי's opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי allows renting houses but not fields in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Fields have two problems and houses do not
steps.stepSummary: Fields carry two problems, so the rabbis made a גזירה against renting them. Houses do not, so they made no גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fields, which have two problems: the rabbis made a decree about them. Houses, which do not have two problems: the rabbis did not make a decree about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same 'two problems' idea it used earlier. Fields are forbidden to rent and houses are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting land in ארץ ישראל is only forbidden by a rabbinic גזירה. The rabbis made that גזירה only where there are two problems, which is true of fields. Houses have only one problem, so רבי יוסי allows renting them.

phrases.english: Fields, which have two problems —
the rabbis made a decree about them;
houses, which do not have two problems —
the rabbis did not make a decree about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rabbis made a גזירה against renting fields because fields have two problems. Houses do not, so renting them stays allowed.

steps.title: Why may houses be sold in סוריא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's rule for סוריא and asks its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in סוריא one may sell, and so on. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of רבי יוסי's opinion, about סוריא, and asks why. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In סוריא, רבי יוסי allows selling houses, not just renting them, but he still forbids selling fields. The גמרא asks what lies behind this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Syria, a land next to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And in Syria one may sell, etc.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next location in רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי allows selling houses in סוריא but not fields.

steps.title: רבי יוסי holds that סוריא is not truly conquered land
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds כיבוש יחיד לא שמיה כיבוש, so סוריא does not count as conquered land. Only fields, with their two problems, are under a גזירה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the conquest of an individual is not called a conquest. A field, which has two problems: the rabbis made a decree about it. Houses, which do not have two problems: the rabbis did not make a decree about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר about whether סוריא counts as conquered land. Because it does not count, only fields are restricted there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since סוריא was conquered by one person, דוד, and not by the whole nation, רבי יוסי says it does not have the status of ארץ ישראל. So there is no Torah-level ban on selling there, only a rabbinic גזירה. That גזירה covers fields, which have two problems, and not houses.

keyTerms.meaning: a conquest by one individual (not the whole nation)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the opposite of step 14. There, רבי מאיר held כיבוש יחיד שמיה כיבוש, meaning it does count as a conquest. Here רבי יוסי holds it does NOT count, and that is why he is more lenient in סוריא.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: כִּיבּוּשׁ יָחִיד לָא שְׁמֵיהּ כִּיבּוּשׁ,
phrases.english: He holds: the conquest of an individual is not called a conquest;
and a field, which has two problems —
the rabbis made a decree about it;
houses, which do not have two problems —
the rabbis did not make a decree about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: כִּיבּוּשׁ יָחִיד לָא שְׁמֵיהּ כִּיבּוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19, using the reverse of רבי מאיר's view from step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סוריא is not conquered land for רבי יוסי, so only a rabbinic גזירה applies there, and it covers fields but not houses.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about סוריא depends on whether כיבוש יחיד counts as a real conquest.

steps.title: Why is everything allowed outside the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's rule for חוץ לארץ and asks its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And outside the land one may sell, and so on. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last part of רבי יוסי's opinion, which allows selling even fields outside the land, and asks why. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fields have two problems in ארץ ישראל, and רבי מאיר used that to forbid selling fields even in חוץ לארץ. So it seems רבי יוסי should also have a גזירה there, as he does in סוריא. The גמרא asks why he does not.

phrases.english: And outside the land one may sell, etc.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third location in רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why even fields may be sold outside the land, unlike in סוריא.

steps.title: Far from the land, the rabbis made no decree
steps.stepSummary: Because חוץ לארץ is far from ארץ ישראל, the rabbis did not make a גזירה there at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is far away, we do not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that distance makes the difference. Land far from ארץ ישראל gets no גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוריא borders ארץ ישראל, so people might confuse the two. That is why the rabbis protected it with a גזירה on fields. Lands far away carry no such risk, so even fields may be sold there.

phrases.english: Since it is far away,
we do not make a decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Distance from ארץ ישראל removes the need for any גזירה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's three levels: in ארץ ישראל, rent houses only. In סוריא, sell houses and rent fields. In חוץ לארץ, sell everything.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling. In practice we follow רבי יוסי's opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of the opinions in the משנה, רבי יוסי's is the one that becomes law. That includes his leniency of selling houses and fields outside the land.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the opinion that steps 17 to 22 explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice we follow רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רב יוסף's limit: do not create a שכונה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds a condition: the leniency applies only as long as one does not turn the place into a non-Jewish שכונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: And only as long as he does not make it a settlement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף limits the ruling just given. You may sell or rent, but not in a way that creates a non-Jewish neighborhood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even where רבי יוסי allows dealing with non-Jews, selling to enough of them to form a group living together is not allowed. This adds a new limit on top of the general permission.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
And provided that he does not make it a settlement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the ruling of step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The permission to sell or rent does not extend to creating a non-Jewish שכונה.

steps.title: How many people make a שכונה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many people count as a שכונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many make a settlement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the word שכונה that רב יוסף just used. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To apply רב יוסף's limit, we need to know the number of people at which a group becomes a שכונה.

phrases.english: And how many people make a settlement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term used in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The smallest number of people that counts as a שכונה.

steps.title: A שכונה is at least three people
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a שכונה is never fewer than three people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A settlement is not less than three people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: three people make a שכונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So selling or renting to one or two non-Jews is fine. Once three would live there together, it becomes a שכונה, which רב יוסף forbids.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, but you may not create a non-Jewish שכונה, which means three or more people.

phrases.english: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שְׁכוּנָה פְּחוּתָה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: A settlement is not fewer than three people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֵין שְׁכוּנָה פְּחוּתָה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שכונה is three or more people.

steps.title: What if another seller adds two more non-Jews?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's condition: one Jew sells to one non-Jew, then another seller sells to two more, and together they form a שכונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should worry: maybe this Jew will go and sell to one non-Jew, and that other one will go and sell to two more, which makes a group of three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with רב יוסף's rule. Even a sale to a single non-Jew might end up being part of a שכונה of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 taught that a שכונה needs at least three people, so selling to one person seems safe. The challenge is that this one sale, joined with another person's sale to two more, completes the three. So maybe even selling to one should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us be concerned (opens a worry or challenge)

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps
this Jew will go
and sell to one non-Jew,
and that other one will go
phrases.notes: 'That one' is someone else who then sells to two more non-Jews. One plus two makes the three needed for a שכונה.

phrases.english: and sell to two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the definition of a שכונה as three people (step 26) to challenge רב יוסף's condition (step 24).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's condition that a sale is allowed as long as one does not make a שכונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sale to one non-Jew, combined with someone else's sale to two, completes a שכונה. So even a single sale should be forbidden.

steps.title: We are warned only about direct causing, not causing from two steps away
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the איסור of לפני עור covers putting a stumbling block before someone directly, not causing it in a chain of steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We are commanded about 'before' the blind, but we are not commanded about 'before' someone who may later put it 'before' the blind.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the worry. The first seller is not responsible for what someone else might do later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור of לפני עור applies when my own action directly leads to the wrongdoing. Here the first seller sells to only one person, and the שכונה happens only if someone else decides to sell to two more. That is too far removed from his act, so he is not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The איסור against putting a stumbling block before the blind, meaning causing someone else to sin (ויקרא 19:14)
'Before the before': causing something two steps away

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of לפני עור covers only direct causing. A chain where someone else must act first (לפני דלפני) is not included, so one may sell to a single non-Jew.
steps.whyThisMatters: אביי's principle of 'לפני דלפני' is a general rule that limits how far responsibility for causing a sin reaches.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We are commanded about 'before,'
phrases.notes: This points to the פסוק 'ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול' (ויקרא 19:14).

phrases.english: we are not commanded about 'before' of 'before.'
phrases.notes: He means causing a sin through someone else's later choice is not covered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the איסור (לפני עור applies only to direct causing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any sale that could end up part of a שכונה should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first seller is only an indirect cause (לפני דלפני), so his sale to one non-Jew is allowed.

steps.title: The משנה's wording implies some places forbid renting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה 'even in a place where they said to rent' and points out that this means there are places where one may not rent at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Even in a place where they said one may rent.' This shows that there is a place where one may not rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה about renting houses to non-Jews. It draws a conclusion from the wording, and this sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' in 'even in a place where they said to rent' only makes sense if other places do not allow renting. So the גמרא learns that renting is forbidden in some places. Next it will need to explain which places those are.

phrases.english: Even in a place where they said to rent.
By inference, there is
a place where they do not rent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section. It moves from the discussion of a שכונה and לפני דלפני (steps 24–28) to the משנה's line about renting houses as a residence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's wording 'even in a place where they said to rent' implies that some places forbid renting to non-Jews altogether.
